subject: Renewal uplift request — aligning mid-contract capacity to Q3 budget window
messages:
From: Sarah Vance <sarah.vance@lumenix.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumenix.io
Date: 2026-06-14T14:05:00Z
Subject: Renewal uplift — aligning to Q3 budget window

Hi Hannah,

Quick note from our side — we ran our Q3 budget planning with finance this morning and have an unexpected burst of capacity need for a new pilot. We currently sit at the mid-tier committed units with Redwood through February 2027. Procurement asked whether we can:

- add a +40% temporary uplift for July–September (mid-contract),
- or convert that uplift into an annualized add-on that co-terms to our existing Feb 1 2027 renewal,
- and what discounts or invoice timing options you can offer for either path.

Important constraints: procurement needs a clear invoice and PO timeline (they prefer PO on or before 2026-07-01), and legal will want a short amendment doc rather than a full SOW. Also — any SLA credit or priority queue assurances for the pilot will be helpful.

Can you map out a short set of options + high-level pricing? We want to present to our CFO by end of next week.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Vance
Head of ML Ops, Lumenix

Subject: Re: Renewal uplift — aligning to Q3 budget window

Hi Sarah — thanks for the context. Forwarding a succinct set of options so procurement/legal have something concrete to review. Attaching an options summary (lumenix-uplift-options-0614.pdf).

High-level options (short):

1) Temporary top-up (fastest)
   - +40% committed units for a 3-month window (Jul–Sep)
   - No change to renewal date (Feb 1 2027)
   - Pricing: list-rate + 6% temporary uplift discount if PO submitted before 2026-07-01
   - Pros: fastest procurement cadence; minimal legal work (amendment)
   - Cons: higher unit price than annualized add-on

2) Annualize + co-term (preferred economics)
   - Convert the uplift into an annual add-on that is amortized to co-term on Feb 1 2027
   - Pricing: blended rate with a 12% volume discount for the uplift portion if committed for the remainder of contract period
   - Pros: lower unit economics; simpler operational routing after Jan; includes one legal amendment to schedule
   - Cons: procurement needs to agree to amend term/pricing now

3) Staged voucher approach (flex, lower upfront)
   - Issue a prepaid voucher equivalent to 70% of projected shortfall; voucher consumed first; remaining usage billed at list with a 8% staging discount
   - Pros: preserves current term, avoids full annualization; easier internal approvals sometimes
   - Cons: accounting treatment may differ for Lumenix; requires invoice timing agreement

SLA & priority: for pilots tied to committed uplift we can offer a one-time SLA credit clause (0.25% monthly credit) and temporary placement in the priority inference queue (subject to capacity OK). We can bake that into the amendment.

Next steps I propose:
- confirm preferred option by 2026-06-18 so we can lock final pricing
- Ben (cc’d) will draft pricing band table and procurement invoice timing options
- Lauren will scope the legal amendment checklist and expected turnaround

If helpful I can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow with procurement and Ben/Lauren to walk through.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Renewals — Redwood Inference

Sarah / Hannah — I ran the numbers and put the uplift bands into a quick CSV (uplift-pricing-band-0615.csv). TL;DR pricing options:

- Temporary top-up (3 months): +40% units charged at list with 6% temporary uplift discount if PO before 2026-07-01
- Annualize & co-term: blended uplift units at 12% discount over the uplift portion for the remainder of the term
- Staged voucher: voucher covers 70% of projected overage; voucher price is list minus 8% staging discount; remaining overage billed at list

Invoice & PO timing notes:
- If procurement can provide PO by 2026-07-01 we can invoice July 1 (or backdate to July 1 on the amendment) and recognize the voucher/amendment in the same invoice run.
- For annualize, we will create a midterm amendment and a pro-rated invoice for the remainder of the term; invoice date can be aligned with PO date (typical turnaround 7–10 business days after signed amendment).

SLA credit recommendation: include 0.25% monthly credit on uplifted units for any SLA breach during the pilot window; needs legal sign-off.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Operations Lead — Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — that breakdown helps. Procurement prefers the staged voucher approach (option 3) because it preserves our current term and accounting path. Two asks before we proceed:

1) can you confirm exact invoice dates & whether the voucher will be a single invoice line item (we prefer a single prepaid invoice),
2) legal needs the amendment template and an explicit SLA credit clause written out,

We anticipate procurement can issue a PO by 2026-07-01; PO will reference the voucher line and our existing contract ID. If you can get the amendment & invoice stub to procurement this week we can move quickly.

Also: is there any possibility of a one-time pilot discount if we commit to convert the voucher to an annual add-on at renewal? That would make our CFO happier.

—Sarah
